decisions.reason: As a classic door lever handle line that is very close to the firm's core architectural hardware knowledge, it is easy for the firm to support, learn from and refine, so withdrawal is unlikely.

This door lever handle family builds directly on the firm's established design, engineering and certification capabilities, which under strong absorptive capacity argues for keeping and improving it rather than dropping it.

Although a single door handle design can be more exposed to portfolio pruning than a broader family, it still sits squarely within the firm's existing knowledge base and can be commercially adjusted with relatively low risk.
This product is close to the firm's longstanding offer and benefits from its in-house R&D, design know-how and market access, making continuation more likely than exit.
A door lever handle family matches the firm's broad system-oriented portfolio and uses capabilities it already possesses, so the firm is likely to keep it and exploit learning effects.

The electronic access system is both close to the firm's existing access-control direction and explicitly presented as a flagship, so a large R&D-active firm would almost certainly retain it and invest in further development.
